samples.summary: `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` lookup walks the prototype chain, so `alignment` values like `toString`/`constructor`/`valueOf` bypass the `?? 'left'` fallback
samples.evidence: `const align = DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left';` uses a plain object literal (not `Object.create(null)`, no `hasOwnProperty` check). For `style.alignment === 'toString'` the lookup returns `Object.prototype.toString` (a function, not undefined), so `??` never fires and `align !== 'left'` is true — the exporter interpolates `<w:jc w:val="function toString() { [native code] }"/>` into word/document.xml, i.e. exactly the non-ST_Jc value the closed map was introduced to prevent. Same for `'__proto__'` → `[object Object]`. The new backend guard (docs-content.controller.ts:266) blocks these over the PUT API, but the CRDT can be written directly by the frontend/importers, so the exporter's own clamp is still the last line of defense.

samples.summary: New block-style value validation covers only `alignment`; the numeric BlockStyle fields still accept arbitrary values that become NaN in layout
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` validates `style.alignment` only. `writeDocsRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:145) writes `marginTop: String(style.marginTop)` verbatim, and the read path does `partial.marginTop = Number(attrs.marginTop)` (docs-tree.ts:160) with `normalizeBlockStyle` being a bare spread (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274, no numeric coercion/guard). A PUT with `style: { marginTop: "abc" }` therefore lands NaN in the model, and `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:383` does `y += block.style.marginTop`, NaN-ing the cumulative y for every subsequent block — the whole document renders blank/garbled for every collaborator, with no way to fix it from the UI. Same exposure for `marginBottom`, `lineHeight`, `textIndent`, `marginLeft`.
searchedFor: grep writeDocsRoot|assertValidDocsBody across packages/backend/src to enumerate write paths

samples.summary: `m?.color ?? firstInline?.color` still treats a cleared marker color ('') as a set value, so the marker ignores the run color it should inherit
samples.evidence: The change replaced the comment that justified `??` (which claimed `StoredColor` has no falsy legal value) with one acknowledging '' is reachable, but kept `??`. With `marker.color === ''` (the #728 reset shape) the expression yields `''`, `resolveStoredColor` maps it to undefined, and the marker paints `theme.defaultColor` — silently discarding `firstInline.color`, which is the value the same '' -means-unset rule says should win. The fallback chain should use the same emptiness test the resolver uses.

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` treats an empty/whitespace alpha component as fully transparent and drops the color
samples.evidence: `isTransparentAlpha` computes `Number(a)`; `Number('')` and `Number(' ')` are `0`, which is finite and `<= 0`, so `rgba(255, 0, 0, )` (or `rgba(255,0,0,\t)`) returns `undefined` and the exporter drops a fully opaque red. The comment on `isTransparentAlpha` states the opposite intent — 'anything unparseable is treated as opaque'. Guard with a check that the alpha text is non-empty before the numeric test.

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` silently drops several CSS color syntaxes that reach `style.color` via HTML paste, losing user-visible color on DOCX/PPTX export
samples.evidence: The regex only accepts comma-separated numeric `rgb()/rgba()`. Percentage channels (`rgb(100%, 0%, 0%)`), the modern space-separated form (`rgb(255 0 0 / 50%)`), `hsl()/hsla()`, `color(srgb ...)` and named colors all fall through to `return undefined`, so `buildRunPropertiesXml` / the PPTX `storedColorToThemeColor` emit no color at all and the run silently reverts to the document/theme default. `view/clipboard.ts:150-154` copies `el.style.color` from pasted HTML, which is where these forms enter the model; the previous code at least round-tripped them (invalidly), the new code loses them outright.

verdict.reason: Verified the full chain and found no guard at any hop. (1) assertValidBlockStyle (docs-content.controller.ts:266-279) validates only style.alignment; assertValidBlock (:281-334) checks id/type/style-is-object/inlines/tableData shape and no numeric field — repo-wide grep for numeric type checks in packages/backend/src returns nothing. (2) The global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-70) cannot help because the route takes `@Body() body: unknown` (controller:124), so the metatype is Object and validation is skipped; no DTO exists for this route. (3) serializeBlockStyle (yorkie/docs-tree.ts:139-150) writes `marginTop: String(style.marginTop)` with no coercion, reached via buildBlockNode:241/258 -> buildTreeChildren:296 -> writeDocsRoot:517-538, so "abc" is persisted verbatim into the CRDT tree attributes. (4) Both read paths coerce with bare Number(): backend parseBlockStyle (docs-tree.ts:159-164) and frontend parseBlockStyle (frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:221-226), and normalizeBlockStyle (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) is only `{...DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE, ...style}`, so a present NaN key overrides the default instead of being rejected. Notably the sibling inline-image path DOES guard with Number.isFinite (docs-tree.ts:121-126, yorkie-doc-store.ts:187-188), showing the numeric block-style fields are the unguarded outlier. (5) NaN then flows unguarded into layout: layout.ts:383 `y += block.style.marginTop` (no ?? / isFinite), layout.ts:741 `Math.max(1, block.style.lineHeight ?? 1.5)` (Math.max(1, NaN) === NaN), and pagination.ts:81 `currentY += block.style.marginTop`, so every subsequent block's y becomes NaN. grep isFinite|isNaN across packages/docs/src shows guards only in importers/color/font-size, none on this path. This is a missing-guard / data-corruption bug in the correctness lane: a single PUT with style:{marginTop:"abc"} (or null, or an object) persists state that NaN-cascades the layout for all collaborators. I searched wide (API validator, backend write+read, frontend write+read, normalize, layout, pagination, global pipes, yorkie.types.ts) and found no counterexample.

finding.summary: Cell-style attribute removal uses a *range* over the whole cell subtree, so `backgroundColor` is also stripped from every inline (text highlight) and nested-table node inside the cell
finding.evidence: `applyCellStyle` now does `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, removeAttrs)` with `endPath = [...cellPath]` and last index +1 — a position range that spans the cell node AND all of its descendants (blocks, inlines, nested tables). Yorkie's tree style/removeStyle applies to every non-text node in the range (the same reason `setBlockType`'s `removeStyleByPath(blockPath, blockPath+1, ['listKind','listLevel'])` at line 1439 reaches inline nodes too — harmlessly, because those keys don't exist there). Here the attribute name collides: inline nodes store text highlight under the very same key `backgroundColor` (`serializeInlineStyle` line 122, `parseInlineStyle` line 177), and nested table cells store `backgroundColor`/`border*`/`padding`. So the new "No fill" reset (docs-table-context-menu.tsx:233 → `{ backgroundColor: undefined }`) silently deletes the highlight colour of every run in the cell and the fills/borders of any nested table — irreversible data loss in the CRDT. The in-memory cache is only patched for the cell (`cell.style = merged`), so the loss is invisible until reload/remote sync, and the added test (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2031) uses a cell whose inlines have no `backgroundColor`, so it cannot catch this. A per-node removal (or an explicit `removeStyleByPath` restricted to the cell element only, e.g. by re-setting the descendants' attrs) is needed.

finding.summary: `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` lookup is not actually closed — prototype keys (`toString`, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `valueOf`) resolve to inherited values that get interpolated into `w:jc/@w:val`
finding.evidence: `const align = DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left'` indexes a plain object literal, so the prototype chain is consulted. `style.alignment === 'toString'` yields `Object.prototype.toString` (a function), which is `!== 'left'` and is stringified into `<w:jc w:val="function toString() { [native code] }"/>`; `'__proto__'` yields `[object Object]`. The doc comment above claims `w:jc w:val` "can only ever carry an ST_Jc token", which is false — the result is a schema-invalid `ST_Jc` value that Word can refuse to open, i.e. the exact failure the change set out to prevent. Use `Object.hasOwn(DOCX_ALIGNMENTS, ...)`, a `Map`/`Set`, or `Object.create(null)`. The same pattern exists in the slides sink the comment cites as the model (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79`, `ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`), so it is not clamped there either.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository: DOCX_ALIGNMENTS is a plain object literal (docx-style-map.ts:115-120) indexed with a bare bracket lookup at line 141 (`DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left'`). The prototype chain is consulted, so alignment values 'toString', 'valueOf', 'constructor', 'hasOwnProperty' resolve to inherited functions and '__proto__' resolves to Object.prototype; `??` only filters null/undefined, all are !== 'left', and all are interpolated into `<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>` at line 143, producing schema-invalid ST_Jc values ("function toString() { [native code] }", "[object Object]"). This contradicts the comment at lines 111-113/138-140 asserting the map is closed and w:jc can only carry an ST_Jc token. The new API validation (docs-content.controller.ts:254,270-278) closes only the content-PUT ingress and its own comment (lines 257-264) states the exporter sink must clamp because values also arrive via CRDT/import/older schema; the exporter is invoked unconditionally from docx-exporter.ts:186, so I could not establish unreachability. The cited slides analogue is also unclamped (slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:61-66,79). Impact is malformed OOXML that a viewer can reject — a broken invariant in the guard, squarely in the correctness lane, so no out-of-scope or already-guarded ground applies.
